requirements.title: A binding part starts with CONTAINS and optionally its own PRIVATE statement

requirements.title: Binding accessibility defaults belong to the declaring type definition
requirements.source: 7.5.5 p8; physical PDF 101, printed 87, lines 22-24.
requirements.definition: The default accessibility of a type's type-bound procedures is private when that definition contains a binding-private-stmt and public otherwise. An explicit access-spec on the particular binding overrides this default; absent it, the default of the definition where the binding was declared applies. Component-part PRIVATE, module default PRIVATE and type-name accessibility are not substitutes for binding PRIVATE. Inherited bindings retain original attributes rather than being reset by a child's binding default.

requirements.title: A public binding is accessible through an accessible object
requirements.source: 7.5.5 p9, first sentence; physical PDF 101, printed 87, line 25.
requirements.definition: A public type-bound procedure is accessible via any accessible object of its type. The type name and implementation procedure name need not themselves be accessible to the caller. A public generic can provide access to a private specific without making that private specific binding name directly usable. 'Accessible object' does not waive reference validity, receiver lifetime or argument/interface restrictions.

requirements.title: Private bindings are accessible only in their defining module and descendants
requirements.source: 7.5.5 p9, second sentence; physical PDF 101, printed 87, lines 25-26.
requirements.definition: A private type-bound procedure is accessible only within the module containing its type definition and within that module's descendants. Ordinary client modules and separately defined extension types do not become descendants by USE association or EXTENDS. Inaccessible inherited bindings retain their identity and attributes. Clause 19 separately prohibits a component/binding name appearing where inaccessible, and 4.2 requires reporting capability for that name-scope violation.
